definitions.speedGate: Ordinary mean absolute percentage error over nonzero high-confidence HUD observations; measured at sourceFrame*2 simulation ticks. No temporal shift or denominator floor.
definitions.fittingError: Only the separate calibration score divides by max(20, source HUD km/h), including zero samples.
definitions.displayedError: Same nonzero percentage error after rounding simulated HUD speed to an integer.
definitions.motionWindow: Each rising raw Shift input through the next rising Shift input or clip end. Input windows are interventions, not measured physical drift episodes.
definitions.motionSpeed: Source entry is the most recent HUD sample at/before the press (at most 3 frames old); simulation entry is exact. Loss is max(0, entry-min)/entry. Post-peak loss separately records decline from the window peak to its subsequent minimum, including a launch that accelerates during drift. Speed recovery is first return to entry speed after the local minimum, not slip recovery.
definitions.responseTiming: Sim events are stamped at the completed 60 Hz tick. Source physical entry, slip recovery, and drift duration are null because only input and inventory events were annotated. Already-held Shift at clip start is not an observed press.
definitions.inventoryTiming: Ordinal same-kind matching without removing large errors. First awards/use in identified launches are controlled comparisons; continuation matching is diagnostic because initial gauge/history are unknown.
definitions.boostCensoring: Timer-active intervals seen in simulated samples. Activity in frame 0 is left-censored/seeded; activity at final sample is right-censored and its duration is only a lower bound. This never establishes original-engine booster duration.
definitions.referenceLimit: Only two held-out launches have identified initial motion. Their 90-tick start buff is a fixed model hypothesis. Beginner footage uses a different source kart. Variable key-overlay latency reaches 100 ms. No whole-video 5% fidelity claim.
definitions.matrixReview: Flags retain the original regression rules. Causal review distinguishes direct attack, following collisions/braking, and incomplete recovery. Reviewed does not mean every reset is unavoidable. Cases no longer flagged by the selected geometry are listed separately.
definitions.itemSeedCaveat: Item draws include trackHash and trackId as well as public seed, slot, box, and pickup tick. Canonical rebaking or geometry changes can change battle histories under the same public seed. Matrix deltas are observed outcome comparisons, not identical-inventory controlled experiments.
definitions.deferredAiContracts: Legacy lane-cost/TTC projection and legacy reported closing speed remain unchanged. Broad corrections and a braking-threshold follow-up failed existing traffic gates and were rejected. A separate actual-closing diagnostic is used only to skip artificial traffic coasting on a grounded, unrestrained, under-speed jump approach without a real closing threat. This narrow exception does not claim to repair the general planner contracts.

baselineIdentity.kind: current harness with original parameter overrides
baselineIdentity.independentSnapshotComparison: Every stored speed and world hash matches the independent fb71b3f simulation snapshot for all 12 clips. The older independent report omits explicit input/frame metadata; video hash, sample counts, and tick grids are independently checked.
baselineIdentity.browserComparison: Separate native browser captures used the independent baseline snapshot and final model. The supplied parity artifact certifies captured states, not unseen portions of the source video.

flags.reviewStatus: confirmed attack/contact chain with unresolved subsequent wall recovery
flags.cause: Selected-fork grip braking is effective: slot 7 enters at 23.857 m/s at 1170. Its missile makes leader 2 airborne at 1176; enemy 1 traps leader 3 at 1186. Slot 7 contacts the newly trapped 3 at 1193 (within the 8-tick input delay), then airborne 2 at 1224. Repeated contacts displace 7 into the outer wall at 1253 at 14.1 m/s while redaction is active 1144–1323. Wall recovery later fails and manual reset occurs 1466. This is combat-induced queue displacement followed by incomplete recovery, not an unavoidable direct-CC reset.

flags.reviewStatus: confirmed self-damage and opponent-CC jump failures; not all direct enemy hits
flags.cause: Slot 2 is hit by its own Token Bomb at tick 1318, stops at s 571.197 (0.192 m before the lip), resumes at 1385 and loses ground at 1394 at 2.266 m/s while applying full throttle/no brake. Token Bomb self damage is explicitly specified. Slot 6 receives slot 7's Bug Report at 1268, resumes 1316 and takes off at 1334 at 5.264 m/s; another enemy airborne hit at 1356 precedes its reset. Jump minimum is 15 m/s. These are self/opponent-CC under-speed departures with insufficient run-up, not synthetic traffic coasting.

flags.reviewStatus: confirmed post-attack route/deck recovery gap; attempted guard rejected without benefit
flags.cause: Opponent airborne at 588–653 carries slot 0 straight through the branch approach. Location changes to the raised graveyard child around 630 at lateral−6.134 m, outside its 4.5 m halfwidth, while physical support is the lower host road. After control returns, the route still targets the child. At 684 the body reaches its footprint but is 0.510 m below the deck, loses host support, and later resets 744. A bounded incoming-child rejection and stricter height-only diagnostic each retained the reset and were rejected; the final locator is unchanged. This post-attack route/height recovery limitation remains.

flags.reviewStatus: confirmed Overclock attack-induced pileup plus following control response
flags.cause: Slot 5 activates Overclock at tick 1195 and its contacts spin slots 3/6/7 at 1218/1224/1232. Slot 6 was also trapped by slot 2 at 1179. The attacker collides with the slowed victims at 1221/1225/1233 and repeatedly with slot 6 afterward. All four leave the jump below vMin 22: slot 3 at 1265/12.465 m/s, slot 7 at 1282/8.170 m/s, slot 6 at 1299/12.064 m/s and slot 5 at 1312/8.082 m/s. Slot 5 has no opponent hit and coasts as a follower at takeoff; this is a self-item-initiated attack/collision/control chain, not unavoidable direct enemy damage to every kart.

actualCombatMatrix.remainingCaveat: All 252 fields and 1134 kart starts finish; there are zero speed-mode resets and zero solo hard contacts. Nine item-mode resets remain: opponent damage, intentional self-Token-Bomb damage, Overclock attack/collision/control chains, and two unresolved post-combat recovery cases (Fernwood wall recovery and Pumpkin route/deck recovery). Four scenarios exceed original per-scenario reset/stall thresholds and remain explicitly flagged. The report does not claim all resets are unavoidable or all acceptance criteria are complete. Item histories also change with trackHash, so baseline/final outcomes are not matched-inventory counterfactuals.

resolvedReviewedCases.originalCause: Enemy Bug Report hits slot 0 at tick 2095 during the warp. The existing impact-speed fix preserves entry speed, but the legitimately active trap zeros movement after the exit at tick 2126. The declared 941 m exit has no supporting triangle; first unsupported tick is 2127, before the later stun at 2193. This is a concrete unsupported exit bug, subsequently repaired locally by placing the exit at 942 m. The focused normal 84-tick trap regression stays stationary and grounded there.

otherReviewedResidualCases.cause: Slot 4 receives opponent Firewall at 1945 and Throttle at 1958. At 2010 it takes off at 18.964 m/s versus jump minimum 26 m/s while applying full throttle and no brake; the active speed cap persists. It misses the 18 m gap and resets 2088. This one-reset scenario does not exceed the baseline reset count but remains visible in total results.
otherReviewedResidualCases.reviewStatus: confirmed opponent speed-loss/cap jump failure; no additional baseline flag

rejectedPostHitRecoveryExperiment.reason: Single scoped recovery experiment was rejected: it repaired Belltower but increased global item-mode respawns 16→18 against its contemporaneous control. No further parameter tuning of that experiment was accepted.

rejectedCommonTimeProjectionExperiment.reason: The common-time gap correction was rejected after full-matrix navigation regressions and an existing traffic-test failure. The delivered policy must not be described as fixing that projection calculation; joint planner calibration is deferred.
